**My thinking, as this farmer:**

I've been working this same land for most of my life. My 5.5 mu rotates wheat and maize every year — wheat goes in October, comes out June, then I immediately put maize in until September. Same as always. My husband's nephew works in the city now so it's mostly me managing, with help at harvest.

For **wheat**, I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station for years — Jimai series. I know it performs well here. After maize harvest I'll hire the rotary tiller — I can't do deep ploughing myself and rotary is cheaper. I apply compound fertilizer at planting (phosphorus and potassium go in at seeding, most people around here do the same), then urea top-dress at jointing. I water four times: the winter water before it freezes, then jointing, heading, and grain filling. If I skip the winter water the plants suffer and I've learned that lesson. I'll spray herbicide in November and do one more spray at jointing for rust and aphids.

For **maize**, I always buy hybrid seed — everyone does, the yield difference is obvious. I direct-seed into the wheat stubble without tilling because it saves time and money in June when there's so much to do. I apply fertilizer twice. Irrigation twice is usually enough if the summer rains come, but I have the well if needed. One pesticide spray for corn borer, maybe two if it's bad.

I'm not changing much from last year. At my age, I stick with what I know works on my land.
